items.title: 2026-015: Critical Vulnerability in Multiple Atlassian Products
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory 2026-015: Atlassian's 5 Oct advisory fixes a critical arbitrary file access flaw across Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira, Bamboo, Crowd, Crucible and Fisheye Data Center. Patch internet-facing instances first and review access logs.

items.title: 2026-014: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory 2026-014: Citrix fixed 8 NetScaler ADC/Gateway flaws, including 2 critical unauthenticated RCEs confirmed exploited in the wild. Update and run compromise assessments on exposed devices.

items.title: 2026-013: Critical Vulnerability in F5 BIG-IP APM
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory 2026-013: F5 disclosed a critical BIG-IP APM vulnerability with confirmed active exploitation; immediate remediation is recommended.

items.title: AI systems are fully capable of carrying out nightmare attacks against infrastructure and nobody's ready
items.summary: Researchers warn AI systems are already capable of executing damaging attacks on critical infrastructure, including moving robotic arms and falsifying OT operator screens, with defences lagging.

items.title: Több ezer olcsó Androidos telefon került forgalomba reklámcsaló vírussal Kutatók több ezer olcsó androidos telefonon találtak előre telepített kártevőt, amely csalárd hirdetési bevételt képes generál…
items.summary: Researchers found pre-installed adware/malware on thousands of low-cost Android phones, generating fraudulent advertising revenue. Supply-chain risk for consumer devices sold in Europe.

items.title: Europol urges early action to protect cryptocurrencies and sensitive data from quantum threats
items.summary: Europol urges organisations to start post-quantum migration now, stressing crypto-agility to protect cryptocurrency and sensitive data regardless of when quantum capabilities arrive.

items.title: AI vulnerability patching has a grading problem
items.summary: Northwestern University tested AI coding agents on 112 real security bugs: a third of patches that stopped the crash still failed maintainer-written tests, questioning autonomous AI vulnerability patching.

items.title: Nippon Columbia malware incident exposes 8.6 million karaoke fan records
items.summary: Daiichi Kosho disclosed that a malware infection at contractor Nippon Columbia exposed over 8.6 million customer and employee records — another third-party supply-chain breach.

items.title: Canadian ransomware negotiator arrested amid FBI hacker crackdown
items.summary: A Canadian ransomware negotiator was arrested as part of an FBI crackdown on hackers, raising insider-risk questions for incident response supply chains.

items.title: Strands Box: Open-source sandbox for AI agents
items.summary: AWS released Strands Box, an open-source sandbox in developer preview that isolates AI agents at the OS level and applies rules based on an agent's prior actions before allowing further operations.

items.title: Energy ceasefire: Confusion in Kyiv, support from allies, silence from Moscow and fresh strikes
items.summary: Trump announced an immediate Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire, unconfirmed by Moscow; Zelenskyy reported fresh Russian strikes on power plants causing outages.

items.title: How can Europe leverage laws to secure cloud sovereignty?
items.summary: Opinion piece on how Europe can use legislation to advance cloud sovereignty without sacrificing speed.

items.title: UK PM Andy Burnham says it is ‘clear’ Russia interfered in 2016 Brexit vote
items.summary: UK PM Andy Burnham publicly stated it is 'clear' Russia interfered in the 2016 Brexit referendum, a first for a sitting UK prime minister.

items.title: Russia strikes power plants in Ukraine despite 'energy ceasefire' announced by Trump
items.summary: Russia struck Ukrainian power plants hours after Trump announced an 'energy ceasefire', keeping energy infrastructure under sustained attack.

items.title: Russian army strikes Sloviansk and Kyiv as Ukrainian drones hit third Yandex data centre
items.summary: Russian strikes hit Sloviansk and Kyiv while Ukrainian drones struck a third Yandex data centre in Vladimir, causing major service outages — data centres increasingly targeted in the conflict.

items.title: Week in review: FortiBleed is still active, Patch Tuesday forecast
items.summary: Help Net Security weekly roundup noting FortiBleed exploitation is still active and previewing the Patch Tuesday forecast, plus healthcare CISO guidance.

items.title: Sweden's Telia to cut around 900 jobs and save $1 million
items.summary: Swedish operator Telia announced around 900 job cuts as part of cost savings, per Reuters.

items.title: The EU budget battle just got nastier
items.summary: Germany rejected Ireland's proposal for the EU's next seven-year budget despite €159bn in cuts, with governments split and Parliament threatening to block the deal.

items.title: What makes some open source updates so difficult?
items.summary: A Google case study estimates most updates of internal open source package copies take four engineering hours or less, but some require days or months — relevant for dependency and patch planning.

items.title: Wie Trumps Ölkrise zur Ukraine-Frage wird
items.summary: German-language analysis of Trump's announced 'energy ceasefire' between Ukraine and Russia, easing of Russia sanctions over oil prices, and his call for new Ukrainian leadership.

items.title: Saudi Arabia says 1 dead, 11 injured in latest attack on Riyadh airport
items.summary: An attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport killed one and injured 11.

items.title: Taiwan says it is closely monitoring series of Chinese live-fire drills
items.summary: Taiwan says it is closely monitoring a series of Chinese live-fire drills.

items.title: ISC Stormcast For Monday, October 12th, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10132, (Mon, Oct 12th)
items.summary: SANS Internet Storm Center daily Stormcast podcast episode for 12 October 2026.

items.title: Trump faces growing backlash over plans to import diesel from Russia
items.summary: Trump faces bipartisan criticism over plans to import Russian diesel ahead of US midterms.

items.title: Ireland’s budget cuts weaken EU, Commission warns
items.summary: The European Commission warns Ireland's proposed long-term budget cuts hit competitiveness and flexibility priorities and weaken the EU.

items.title: Parliament split on EU climate rules opens way for conservative deal with far right
items.summary: The European Parliament is split over EU climate rules, potentially pushing conservatives toward a deal with the far right on the carbon market.

items.title: Europeans back Zelenskyy after Trump calls for new Ukrainian leader
items.summary: Several European governments reaffirmed support for Zelenskyy after Trump called for new Ukrainian leadership.

items.title: Fix airport queues by Christmas, migration commissioner tells Brussels Airport
items.summary: EU migration commissioner Brunner pressed Brussels Airport to resolve Entry/Exit System queues by Christmas, saying member states had enough time to prepare.

items.title: 'Up to our people' to pick leader, Zelenskyy responds to Trump's pledge for new elections in Ukraine
items.summary: Zelenskyy responded to Trump's call for new Ukrainian elections, saying leadership choice is up to Ukrainians and that Russia alone is responsible for the war.

items.title: Man who planned to attack Poland's prime minister has been arrested, interior minister says
items.summary: Polish authorities arrested a man suspected of planning an attack on PM Tusk and the defence minister.

items.title: Python 3.15.0 added to actions/python-versions
items.summary: Python 3.15.0 is now available in actions/python-versions, enabling GitHub Actions test matrices against the new stable release.
